raconter.name: Tell it in full
raconter.phrase: Simple questions to find the details that went missing.
raconter.intro: We'll go back through your dream together, slowly. A few questions to find its pieces again.

film.q: Tell me this dream, like a film. Take your time.
film.placeholder: i was in a house i didn't know…

details.q: Which details come back sharp? A colour, a sound, a smell?

corps.q: Close your eyes a moment. What does this dream do in your body?
corps.hint: no need to name it — just the feeling

reel.q: Could it be real? This place, these people — do you know them?

rappelle.q: Does it remind you of something? Another dream, a recent moment?

garde.q: Out of all that, what do you want to keep for today?

retour.name: Go back into the dream
retour.phrase: Close your eyes and revisit your dream, awake, to see what comes next.
retour.intro: Eyes closed, you'll go back into your dream — just to see what happens there if you stay a while.

installe.q: Settle in. Close your eyes, breathe a few times. Let the day go.

revois.q: See the strongest image of the dream again. Only that one. Let it come back.

entre.q: Step into the image, eyes closed. Look around. Let what follows come, without forcing.

depose.q: When it stops on its own, come back gently. Write what came — even three words.
depose.placeholder: what i saw, what i felt…

geste.name: One small real action
geste.phrase: Carry your dream into a small real action: draw it, write it, put it somewhere.
geste.intro: This dream stayed with you. We'll give it a follow-up in real life — one small thing, doable today.

envie.q: This dream — what does it make you want to do, right now, for real?

choix.q: Choose one small action, doable today. The simplest one.
choix.hint: draw, write a note, call someone, put an object somewhere

quand.q: When will you do it? Write it down — that makes it real.

intention.name: An intention for the night
intention.phrase: Before sleep: ask your night a question.
intention.intro: Before you fall asleep, we'll get the night ready. You'll hand a question to your sleep.

journee.q: Your day in one sentence? Quick — no need to say it well.

question.q: A question you'd like to ask your night?
question.placeholder: what do i need to know about…

image.q: An image that could go with you as you fall asleep?
image.hint: a door, a face, a light — whatever comes

confie.q: Say your question quietly, one last time. Then let it go.

rendormir.name: Fall back asleep gently
rendormir.phrase: After a bad dream or a rough waking: come back to calm.
rendormir.intro: You woke up shaken. That's ok. We'll come back to calm, slowly, together.

ici.q: Feel the bed under you, the blanket, the air on your skin. You're here, safe.

respire.q: Breathe slowly. In… hold a moment… out, longer. Twice more.

main.q: The bad dream isn't here anymore. Put a hand on your chest if that helps.

lieu.q: Think of a place where you feel good. Picture it around you, in detail.
lieu.placeholder: a beach, a childhood room… (or keep it to yourself)

laisse.q: Let your eyes close. Nothing more to do. Sleep comes back on its own.

relire.name: Go back over your day
relire.phrase: 5 minutes in the evening to replay the day.
relire.intro: We'll replay the film of your day, quietly, before the night.

passe.q: What happened today? Someone you met, a moment, a question?

corps.q: How does your body carry this day? Where is it tight, where is it calm?

echo.q: Does a moment from today echo a recent dream?

coinc.q: Was there an odd coincidence today?

endors.q: What would you like to fall asleep with tonight? An image, a word?

ecouter-corps.name: Listen to your body
ecouter-corps.phrase: Where it settles in your body, and what it's asking for.
ecouter-corps.intro: We'll listen to your body for a moment. It often knows things before the head does.

ou.q: This dream, or this moment — where do you feel it in your body?

quoi.q: This feeling — what is it? Warm, cold, tight, light, heavy?

mot.q: If you had to put one single word on it, which one?

demande.q: Stay with it a moment. What would this feeling want?
demande.hint: wait a few seconds in silence, then write what comes
demande.placeholder: to be left alone, to be listened to…

parler-image.name: Talk to an image
parler-image.phrase: Choose one image from the dream and let it answer.
parler-image.intro: We'll pick one image from your dream and let it talk to you. Yes, it works better than you'd think.

choix.q: Choose an image from your dream. The first one that comes. Which one?
choix.placeholder: the door, the dog, the river…

decris.q: Describe it, as if I couldn't see it. Colours, shape, details.
decris.placeholder: it's big, dark, it moves a little…

dit.q: Look at it a moment. If it could speak, what would it say to you?
dit.hint: let it come, even if it feels made up

reponds.q: And you — what do you want to answer it?

coincidence.name: Tell the coincidence
coincidence.phrase: Lay out what happened, in order — that often clears it up on its own.
coincidence.intro: We'll lay out this coincidence, start to finish. Often, telling it is enough to light it up.

ordre.q: Tell me what happened. In order, from start to finish.

avant.q: What were you doing, or thinking, just before?

touche.q: What did it touch in you, in the moment?

histoire.q: If you tell all of that as one single story, how does it go?

intuition.name: Catch an intuition
intuition.phrase: Write down what just went through you, before it flies off.
intuition.intro: Something just went through you. Let's catch it quickly, before it's gone.

note.q: Write down fast what just went through you. Don't look for the right words.

contexte.q: Where were you, what were you doing when it came?

ressemble.q: What did it feel like? An image, a sentence, a sensation?

kairos.bubble: A kairos is a moment that counts — not just any instant, the one that marks you.
body: In the app we say « moment ». But its real name is kairos.
A kairos isn’t what time it is. It’s an instant with weight: a strong dream, an unsettling coincidence, a shiver, an intuition that lands all at once.
We keep the word for a simple reason. Most of our instants slip past unnoticed. A few don’t. Those are worth stopping for.
Every time you write something into Dream, you catch a kairos before it fades. Over time, they draw a map of what actually touches you.
kairos.source: Where it comes from: the ancient Greeks had two words for time. Chronos, the time that passes, minute after minute. And kairos, the right moment — the one you shouldn’t let slip.

intuition.bubble: An intuition is an idea or an image that arrives on its own, without you looking for it.
body: An intuition is an idea or an image that arrives on its own. You weren’t looking for it: it’s there.
In the shower, walking, driving. Often it brings an answer — sometimes a question.
Artists and scientists say their best ideas arrive like that, when they aren’t forcing.
Dream simply offers to write them down. Looking back, you’ll see which ones were right.
intuition.source: Where it comes from: dreamers in every era have noticed that the mind keeps working when you aren’t watching it. (For the curious: Gaston Bachelard wrote beautiful pages on reverie.)

signe.bubble: A sign is something ordinary that suddenly takes on a particular meaning — for you.
body: A bird that lands, a word that comes back three times in a day, a song at the right moment.
Nothing magic in itself. What counts is that it speaks to you, now.
Dream will never tell you « this means that ». A sign has no fixed meaning: it has the meaning you give it, at the moment you notice it.
Writing it down keeps a trace of those instants when the world seemed to wink at you. Reading them back later, you’ll sometimes see a thread you missed at the time.
signe.source: Where it comes from: in almost every culture, people have paid attention to signs. That isn’t believing anything at all — it’s staying awake to what touches us.

coincidence.bubble: A coincidence is two things happening together that, side by side, seem to mean something.
body: You think of someone, they call. You dream of a place, you walk past it the next day.
Most of the time it’s chance. But some coincidences stay with us, because they land exactly when we were asking a question.
Dream doesn’t claim a coincidence is a message. It simply offers to tell it in the order it happened — often, that alone lights up what it stirred in you.
coincidence.source: Where it comes from: a Swiss psychiatrist, Carl Jung, gave a name to coincidences that seem to carry meaning: « synchronicity ». He didn’t say they were magic, only that they were worth looking at.

frisson.bubble: A shiver is what the body does when something lands exactly right.
body: Goosebumps at a piece of music, a memory that tightens your throat, a sentence that goes straight through you.
The body often reacts before the words. The shiver is its way of saying « yes, this one matters ».
Many people describe that shiver at the moment something rings true for them.
Dream offers to note when it happens, and in front of what. Over time, you spot what moves you — what actually counts for you.
frisson.source: Where it comes from: it has long been observed that the body knows things before the head does. Listening to your shivers is listening to that part.

sieste.bubble: A nap isn’t only rest: it’s a good moment to catch images as they pass.
body: Just before you fall asleep, or just as you wake, the mind makes strange free images, between the day and the dream.
Those images go fast. A short nap is a fine chance to pick them.
The painter Salvador Dalí took very short naps to catch these in-between images, before dropping into deep sleep.
If you write a moment down just after a nap, tell Dream: those images are often among the most surprising.
sieste.source: Where it comes from: this in-between state, between waking and sleep, has a name: hypnagogia. Many creators have used it on purpose to find new ideas.

how-interpret.bubble: The more you say what you see, the more Dream learns YOUR language — and the more its readings sound like you.
body: Dream always starts with you. Before offering anything, it asks what you see in your dream.
Your reading counts most. That’s the one Dream keeps first.
Then, and only then, it offers its own: what stands out, a possible link with your life, a question to close. Never a verdict. Always « here’s a track », never « here’s what it means ».
Dream doesn’t read from a dream dictionary. Water, for you, doesn’t mean what it means for someone else. It’s YOUR meaning being built here, dream after dream.
how-interpret.source: Where it comes from: many people who work with dreams share the same rule — the one who dreamt stays the only owner of the meaning. The other’s job is to help search, not to decide.

wall-anon.bubble: On the Wall, nobody knows it’s you. Not even your groups. You can take your dream back whenever you want.
body: The Wall is where dreams are shared without names. You can share one, and read the others.
When you share on the Wall, what you write becomes anonymous. Your name doesn’t appear. Your groups don’t know it’s you. Nobody can trace it back to your account.
You stay in control: at any moment, in Settings, you can take one of your dreams off the Wall. It disappears.
The Wall renews itself at its own pace, each time you open it. Nothing to refresh, nothing to keep running.
wall-anon.source: Where it comes from: sharing a dream without saying who you are is an old idea. It lets you be true without feeling exposed.

credits.bubble: Creating images or worlds costs real computing power. Credits pay for that — nothing else.
body: Writing your dreams, understanding them, keeping them: that’s the heart of Dream, and it costs no credits.
Credits are only used when you ask the Forge to create something heavy: an image, a world, a piece of work made from your dream.
Those creations run on large computers that use a lot of energy. Credits cover that real cost. It isn’t play money.
No traps: no countdown, no « offer expiring soon ». You top up when you want, and you always see what you’re paying for and why.
credits.source: Where it comes from: we’d rather tell you plainly what your money pays for than hide it inside a vague subscription.

data.bubble: Your dreams stay yours: nothing is erased except by you, and you can take everything with you whenever you want.
body: What you write in Dream belongs to you: your dreams, your moments, your notes.
Nothing erases itself. Nothing goes to a group or to the Wall unless you decide it.
You can get it all back. « Export everything » gives you a file with everything you’ve written, to keep wherever you want.
And you can leave for good. « Delete my account » erases your data. As a safety net, we wait seven days before the final erasure, in case you change your mind — you can cancel during that time.
data.source: Where it comes from: we think a dream is an intimate thing. You should be able to keep it, take it with you or erase it without asking permission.

guide-image.bubble: You choose one image from your dream, and let it answer you, as if it could speak.
body: In a dream, one image often comes back: a door, an animal, a person, an object.
This guide invites you to speak to it. Not as a game — to see what comes when you let it « answer ».
You ask a simple question: who are you? what do you want? Then you listen to what rises, without forcing.
Often the image says something you already knew, without the words. It surprises, and it clears things up.
guide-image.source: Where it comes from: people who work with dreams invite us to treat images as alive, rather than as symbols to decode. It’s sometimes called « letting the dream go on ».

guide-corps.bubble: You look at where the dream settles in your body, and what that place seems to be asking for.
body: A dream often leaves a physical trace: a tight throat, a knotted belly, a warmth, a weight on the chest.
This guide invites you to put your attention there, gently, without trying to change anything.
You name what you feel, and you wait. Sometimes the feeling moves on its own once it’s really looked at.
This is not care and not treatment. It’s a way of listening to yourself, and it’s often enough to see more clearly.
guide-corps.source: Where it comes from: an American psychologist, Eugene Gendlin, noticed that paying attention to what you feel in the body often helps you understand what’s working on you. He called it « focusing ».

guide-intuition.bubble: You write down what just went through you — an idea, an image — before it flies off.
body: Intuitions don’t announce themselves and they don’t stay. A few seconds, and it’s already blurred.
This guide is very short: it helps you put down what comes right away, without judging it, without sorting it.
You say what you saw or thought, even if it makes no sense in the moment.
Later, reading back, you’ll see which ones were right. That’s how you learn to trust your intuitions.
guide-intuition.source: Where it comes from: that state where ideas arrive freely, between waking and sleep or in full reverie, has interested creators forever. It’s been called reverie, or hypnagogia.

guide-reentry.bubble: You close your eyes, awake, and go back into your dream to see what happens next.
body: A dream often stops at the wrong moment: just before the end, on a closed door, a question left hanging.
This guide offers to pick it up again, awake, eyes closed. You put yourself back in the scene and let what follows come.
Nothing has to happen. Sometimes the scene moves, sometimes not. Both are fine.
It’s a gentle way to stay a while with a dream that marked you, instead of letting it slip away.
guide-reentry.source: Where it comes from: picking a dream back up while awake, to let it go further, is an old practice, used in several traditions to listen better to what the dream had to say.

guide-intention.bubble: Before sleep, you put a question or an intention to your night.
body: You can go into sleep with a small question in mind: about a choice, an emotion, a dream that keeps coming back.
This guide helps you put it simply, in one sentence, just before you fall asleep.
It doesn’t command dreams — nobody can do that. But it points your attention, and sometimes the night answers in its own way.
In the morning, you write down what came, even a fragment. Over time, you’ll see whether your night likes being spoken to.
guide-intention.source: Where it comes from: asking something of your night before sleeping is a very old practice, found in many cultures. It’s sometimes called dream « incubation ».

signal-soin.bubble: Dream predicts nothing. It notices when your dream presses on the same thing several times.
body: Sometimes a dream insists. The same argument coming back, something breaking, a body that can’t go on, something left behind — scene after scene.
When it’s clear, Dream tells you. Once. Without drama.
This is not a prediction. Your dream is not announcing an accident, a breakup or an illness, and Dream won’t either. It makes no diagnosis: it is not a medical tool.
What it does: name what comes back in the dream. Nothing more. What that touches in your life — you’re the one who knows, or nobody does.
You can wave the card away. It won’t come looking for you: at most one a week, never more.
And if what you write speaks of real distress — dark thoughts, violence, danger — Dream stops commenting. It gives you numbers where someone picks up.
signal-soin.source: Where it comes from: many dreamers notice that a dream can press on what they avoid in the daytime. That doesn’t tell the future. It tells what weighs now.

appointments.title: Dream
appointments.morning: ☾ Sleep well? Tell your dream before it goes.
appointments.evening: ☀ An intention for the night? 30 seconds.

dream.trailAria: what you can put down here
dream.bubbleLead: Under “dream” there’s more than dreams. All of this belongs here:
pageIntro: Under the word “dream” there’s more than dreams. There’s everything that reaches you without being asked for — at night, and in daylight too.
You don’t have to sort anything in the moment. You put it down; the app asks afterwards.

reve: Whole or in pieces. Three blurry images are worth as much as a full story — and they’re the usual case.
No dream is too small, or too silly. A door that won’t shut counts as much as a dream where you fly.
The best moment is on waking, before coffee. After that, it leaves.
signe: A crow that lands. A word that comes back three times in a day. A sentence overheard on the bus, right on the thing you’ve been chewing over all week.
Nothing magic in itself. What matters is that it caught you, on that particular day.
Dream will never tell you what it means — a sign has no fixed meaning. But note enough of them and yours start to form a language only you speak.
reverie: Eyes open. On the train, in the shower, looking out of a window — and you’re somewhere else.
We take it for a failed dream, or for wasted time. It’s another thing altogether: a waking mode, where the images arrive without being fetched.
Write it down the way it came. The image, not the explanation.
hypnagogie: Just before you drop off, or just after you surface. A face. A sentence heard very clearly. Shapes that move.
It lasts a few seconds and it nearly always dissolves.
If you catch one, write fast: two words will do.
frisson: Goosebumps on a piece of music. The throat tightening. The thing that goes through you when someone says something true.
Often the body has answered before you’ve worked out what to.
You can note only that: when it happened, and in front of what. That’s already a deposit.
synchronicite: You think of someone, they call. You dream of a place, you walk past it the next day.
Most of the time it’s chance, and Dream will never claim otherwise. But some land exactly when you were asking the question — those ones you still remember ten years on.
It announces nothing. Tell it in the order it happened: that’s usually where it clears up on its own.
note_jour: Whatever fits no box. A sentence from the day. Something that gripped you. A joy.
It’s the way out of all the others: when it looks like none of the above, put it here.

after: Nothing is required. A deposit that stays a deposit is all we ask of you.

But if you want to go further with one of them, Dream has small crossings: a few questions, one at a time, five minutes. There’s one for listening to your body, one for going back into an interrupted dream, one for telling a coincidence.
dream.source: Where this comes from: kairos is a Greek word — the right moment, the one you don’t want to let slip. Robert Moss made an everyday practice of it: reading the signs of the day the way you’d read a dream. The word synchronicity comes from Carl Jung, who didn’t say those coincidences were magic, only that they were worth looking at. Gaston Bachelard wrote a whole book defending reverie, which people took for wasted time. And the researcher Harry Hunt showed there isn’t one kind of dream but several — which is why there’s more than one box here.

heart.bubbleLead: The word, the song, the cry, the murmur. Whatever your heart has to say, right now:
rows: a doubt, a decision that weighs
or nothing in particular — just how it’s going
heart.pageTitle: What the heart is allowed to say
pageIntro: There’s no right answer to “how are you feeling”. There’s yours, today, however it comes out.
You record it for yourself first. Nothing goes anywhere until you decide it does.

joie.title: a joy
body: It deserves saying as much as the rest. We note what’s stuck and forget to keep what’s going well — six months later, none of it is left.

peur.title: a fear, a doubt
body: The thing keeping you awake. The decision you’ve been putting off for three weeks.
Saying it out loud doesn’t settle it. It gives it its real size.

colere.title: an anger, a cry
body: The rage that found nowhere to go. The unfairness you swallowed without saying anything.
It’s allowed to exist here, with nobody asking you to calm it down first.

douleur.title: a pain
body: What hurts. Nobody here will tell you it’s nothing, or that it’ll pass.
You put it down, and it’s kept.

gratitude.title: a gratitude
body: Thank you to whom, thank you for what. It comes out clumsily — here, it’s allowed to come out clumsily.

rien.title: or nothing in particular
body: Some days there’s no news. “I’m fine, it’s flat” is a valid deposit.
Read back in three months, it will say something.

after: After a deposit, Dream offers to talk with you about what you’ve just said. You can also do nothing: having said it is already something.
And if you want a guided crossing, there are evening ones — going back over your day, setting an intention before sleep, falling back asleep when the night has broken.
